also: it’s only a few steps away

terms.grammar: ablative of measure with abesse or distāre; the accusative, paucōs passūs, is as good
evidence: Verg. A. 11.907: nec longīs inter sē passibus absunt
Caes. BG 1.22.1: ipse ab hostium castrīs nōn longius mīlle et quīngentīs passibus abesset
terms.comment: Latin measures the distance in paces, as it measured its miles in mīlia passuum; Vergil says of two columns that they are “not many paces apart”.

phrases.latin: Pistrīna paucīs passibus abest; pedibus eāmus.
phrases.english: The bakery is only a few steps away; let’s walk.
Go forward a few steps and stop.

phrases.latin: sīc ambō ad mūrōs rapidī tōtōque feruntur agmine nec longīs inter sē passibus absunt
phrases.english: so both sweep on to the walls with their whole columns, not many paces apart
